findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_tour, get_tour_reviews, get_tour_photos, get_booking_status · Private data: submit_booking_request, create_booking_session, get_booking_status, get_contact, accept_terms, get_order_status, get_documents, send_documents, request_change · Public sink: find_similar_tours, get_tour_photos, submit_booking_request, get_booking_status, get_policies, pay, send_documents, get_payment_options, request_change · Destructive: get_availability, get_tour_dates.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_tour, get_tour_reviews, get_tour_photos, get_booking_status · Private data: submit_booking_request, create_booking_session, get_booking_status, get_contact, accept_terms, get_order_status, get_documents, send_documents, request_change · Public sink: find_similar_tours, get_tour_photos, submit_booking_request, get_booking_status, get_policies, pay, send_documents, get_payment_options, request_change · Destructive: get_availability, get_tour_dates

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

detail: Tool "send_documents" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
